note: FIRST RUN OF THE ENGINE ON A MOBILE GPU, and the first touch-device frame number this repo has (docs/features/mobile-controls.md recorded the gap: 'field-checked headless, not on real hardware — no touch-device frame-time row exists in docs/benchmarks/'). User-run, read off the dispatch console's own status bar on their phone; NOT a `?bench=all` sweep and NOT comparable with any row in index.md — different renderer host, different world, different harness, no p95, no GPU timers (the adapter has no `timestamp-query`). It exists to establish that the engine runs at all on this class of hardware, and to be the baseline a later real sweep replaces. THE WORLD IS SYNTHETIC: `?demo=1` builds a 12x12 grid of block cells with one RGBA8 texture array in-process — no pak, no streaming, no LODs, no water, no vehicles, no peds. A pak from SA assets could not be used because its textures are BC and this GPU has none; that is the whole reason the `--rgba8` converter flag exists, and a district built with it is the run this one is owed a successor to. WHAT MADE IT POSSIBLE: `#enable-unsafe-webgpu` in the browser (it lifts Chromium's adapter blocklist — the default request returned null before it, and the browser had to be restarted for it to take), plus the same day's engine change that stopped REQUIRING texture-compression-bc at device creation. Without either, this device never reaches a frame. The flag is a developer flag, so this measures capability, not a shipping configuration.

device.noBc: texture-compression-bc absent — ASTC and ETC2 present instead
device.noTimestamps: timestamp-query absent, so gpuPassMs/gpuPostMs are unavailable on this device

runs.surface: dispatch console, ?demo=1, opened from a downloaded single-file HTML
runs.note: Map viewport is roughly 360 x 350 CSS px at DPR 2 (the compact layout gives the rest to the call sheet), so the render target is small — a full-screen 3D view would cost more and is not measured here.

comparisonAnchor.sameBuildSameWorldOnSwiftShader: 38-46 fps at 412 x 915 CSS px (emulated Pixel 7, ANGLE/SwiftShader, 2026-08-04)
comparisonAnchor.reading: The software rasterizer in CI and a real Mali-G51 land in the same band, which says the frame is NOT GPU-bound here at this target size — it is bounded by something both share. Do not read that as a Mali-G51 result for a real world; 162 draws over 38 synthetic cells is a fraction of what a streamed district submits (the desktop `map` row submits 393 avg / 680 max).

openQuestions: No p95, so nothing is known about hitching — the number that catches stutter is exactly the one a status bar cannot give.
No GPU timers on this adapter; a real cost breakdown needs a device with timestamp-query or a CPU-side proxy.
Untested at full-screen and at DPR 2 without the sheet taking half the height.

Untested against a real world: the `--rgba8` district pak is the run this one is owed a successor to, and it will also be the first residency figure that means anything (37 MB here is one 64x64 texture array plus 38 block cells).
